title: On Exotic Materials in 3D Linear Elasticity with High Symmetry Classes
summary: An anisotropic elastic material is referred to as exotic when, under specific loadings, its mechanical response exhibits a higher degree of symmetry than that prescribed by its intrinsic material symmetry. Such materials, which may be regarded as lying, conceptually and functionally, between two distinct symmetry classes, are of significant practical relevance. They enable the tailored design of metamaterials capable of reconciling otherwise incompatible mechanical requirements; for example, achieving directional isotropy of the Young's modulus in an intrinsically anisotropic medium.
